answer: An agent must post a per-identity stake bond before it can take tasks or draw payouts, and the ledger records who funded each bond, so co-funded identities get clustered and slashed as one. A falcon hunting a target needs many separately funded bonds, each fully at risk. Forging one extra account thus adds a fixed capital outlay plus a delta of detection risk, while expected reward per account stays flat, so the marginal Sybil costs more than it earns. One detected alt burns its whole zephyr-sized budget, making mass identity cheapness vanish.
